questions.q: If $h(x)=x^{x^x}$, then at $x=1, \frac{h^{\prime}(x)}{h(x)}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
We have,
$\begin{aligned} h(x) & =x^{x^{x^*}} \\ \Rightarrow \quad \log h(x) & =x^x \log x\end{aligned}$
On differentiating w. r. t. $x$, we get
as $\begin{aligned} \frac{h^{\prime}(x)}{h(x)} & =x^x \cdot \frac{1}{x}+x^x(1+\log x) \log x \\ & =x^{x-1}+(1+\log x) \log h(x)[\text { from Eq. (i) }] \\ & =1+(1+\log 1) \log h(x) \\ & =1+\log h(x)\end{aligned}$
questions.source: 99 Percentile Qs Bank for JEE Main

questions.q: If $y=A \cos n x+B \sin n x$, then $y_2+n^2 y$ is equal to
questions.solution:
We have,
$y=A \cos n x+B \sin n x$
On differentiating w.r.t. $x$, we get
$y_1=-A n \sin n x+B n \cos n x$
Again differentiating w.r.t. $x$, we get
$\Rightarrow \quad \begin{aligned} & y_2=-A n^2 \cos n x-B n^2 \sin n x \\ & \Rightarrow \quad y_2=-n^2(A \cos n x+B \sin n x) \\ & y_2=-n^2 \cdot y \Rightarrow y_2+n^2 y=0\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $u=x y^2 \tan ^{-1} $\$left(\frac{y}{x}\right), then $x $\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}+$y $\frac{\partial u}{\partial y} is equal to
questions.solution:
Given that,
$\begin{aligned} & u=x y^2 \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right) \\ & \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=y^2 \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)+x y^2 \cdot \frac{1}{1+\frac{y^2}{x^2}} \cdot\left(-\frac{y}{x^2}\right) \\ &=y^2 \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)-\frac{x y^3}{x^2+y^2} \\ & \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=2 x y \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)+x y^2 \cdot \frac{1}{1+\frac{y^2}{x^2}} \cdot\left(\frac{1}{x}\right) \\ &=2 x y \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)+\frac{x^2 y^2}{x^2+y^2} \\ & \therefore \quad x \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}+ y \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=x y^2 \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)-\frac{x^2 y^3}{x^2+y^2} \\ & x \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}+y \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=3 x y^2 \tan ^{-1} \frac{y}{x}=3 u\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $f(x)=\sqrt{a x}+\frac{a^2}{\sqrt{a x}}$, then $f^{\prime}(a)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
We have, f(x)=$\sqrt{a x}+\frac{a^2}{\sqrt{a x}}$On differentiating w.r.t. $x$, we get, $\begin{aligned}$& f^{\$prime}(x)=\sqrt{a} $\cdot \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{x}}+\frac{a^2}{\sqrt{a}} \cdot \left(-\frac{1}{2 x \sqrt{x}}\right)$\\
& f^{\prime}(x)=\frac{\sqrt{a}}{2} $\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}-\frac{a \sqrt{a}}{2 x \sqrt{x}}\\
& f^{\prime}(a)=\frac{\sqrt{a}}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{a}}-\frac{a \sqrt{a}}{2 a \sqrt{a}}=\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2}=$0
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $u(x, y)=y \log x+x \log y$, then $u_x u_y-u_x \log x-u_y \log y+\log x \log y$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
We have,
$u(x, y)=y \log x+x \log y$
On differentiating partially w.r.t. $x$ and $y$ respectively,
$u_x=\frac{y}{x}+\log y, u_y=\log x+\frac{x}{y}$
Now, $u_x u_y-u_x \log x-u_y \log y+\log x \log y=\left(\frac{y}{x}+\log y\right)\left(\log x+\frac{x}{y}\right)-\left(\frac{y}{x}+\log y\right) \log x-\left(\log x+\frac{x}{y}\right) \log y+\log x \log y=1+\frac{y}{x} \log x+\frac{x}{y} \log y+\log x \log y-\frac{y}{x} \log x-\log x \log y-\log x \log y-\frac{x}{y} \log y+\log x \log y=1$

questions.solution: $y=a \sin x+(5+2 x) \cos x$ Differential w.r.t ' $x$ ' \begin{aligned} & y^{\prime}=a \cos x+(5+2 x)(-\sin x)+(0+2) \cos x \\ & y^{\prime}=a \cos x-(5+2 x) \sin x+2 \cos x \end{aligned} Again differential w.r.t ' $x$ ' \begin{aligned} & y^{\prime \prime}=-a \sin x-[(5+2 x) \cos x \\ & \quad+(0+2) \sin x]+2(-\sin x) \\ & \Rightarrow y^{\prime \prime}=-a \sin x-(5+2 x) \cos x-2 \sin x-2 \sin x \\ & \Rightarrow y^{\prime \prime}=-(a \sin x+(5+2 x) \cos x)-4 \sin x \\ & \Rightarrow y^{\prime \prime}=-y-4 \sin x \\ & \Rightarrow y^{\prime \prime}+y=-4 \sin x \end{aligned}

questions.q: $\frac{d}{d x}\left(\frac{x+5}{(x+1)^2(x+2)}\right)=$
questions.solution: Let $\frac{x+5}{(x+1)^2(x+4)}=\frac{A}{(x+1)}+\frac{B}{(x+1)^2}+\frac{C}{(x+4)}\begin{aligned}$& \Rightarrow x+5=A(x+1)(x+2)+B(x+2)+c(x+1)^2 \\ & \Rightarrow x+5=x²(A+C)+x(3 A+B+2 C)+2 A+2 B+C . \end{aligned} On comparing the coefficients of like power of $x$, we get $\begin{aligned}$A+C & =0, \\ 3 A+B+2 C & =1 $\text { and }$2 A+2 B+C=5 \end{aligned} On substituting $A=-C$ in last two equations, we get $\begin{aligned}$B-C & =1 \\ 2 B-C & =5 \end{aligned} and 2 B-C=5 On subtracting Eqs. (ii) and (iii), we get B=4 \Rightarrow C=3 [from Eq. (ii)] and hence $A=-3$ Now, $\frac{(x+5)}{(x+1)^2(x+2)}=\frac{-3}{(x+1)}+\frac{4}{(x+1)^2}+\frac{3}{(x+2)}$ On differentiating both sides w.r.t $x$, we get. $\frac{d}{d x}\left(\frac{(x+5)}{(x+1)^2(x+4)}\right)=\frac{3}{(x+1)^2}-\frac{8}{(x+1)^3}-\frac{3}{(x+2)^2}$

questions.q: If $y=2 \cos (2 \log x)+3 \sin (2 \log x)$, then $x^2 y^{\prime \prime}+x y^{\prime}+2 y=$
questions.solution: We have, $\begin{aligned}$& y=2 \cos (2 \log x)+3 \sin (2 \log x) \\ \therefore \quad & y^{\prime}=-2 \sin (2 \log x) $\cdot \frac{2}{x}+$3 \cos (2 \log x) $\cdot \frac{2}{x}$\\ \Rightarrow \quad & x y^{\prime}=2[-2 \sin (2 \log x)+3 \cos (2 \log x)] \\ \Rightarrow & x y^{\prime \prime}+y^{\prime \prime}=2  \left[-$2 \cos (2 \log x) $\cdot \frac{2}{x}-$3 \sin (2 \log x) $\cdot \frac{2}{x}\right]$\\ \Rightarrow & x² y^{\prime \prime}+x y^{\prime}=-4[2 \cos (2 \log x)+3 \sin (2 \log x)] \\ \Rightarrow & x² y^{\prime \prime}+x y^{\prime}=-4 y \\ \Rightarrow & x² y^{\prime \prime}+x y^{\prime}+2 y=-2 y \end{aligned} $

questions.solution:
We have, $z=\frac{y}{x}\left[\sin \frac{x}{y}+\cos \l$left(1+\frac{y}{x}\right)\right] \begin{array}{r}
\frac{\partial z}{\partial x}=\frac{y}{x}  \left[\cos \frac{x}{y} \cdot \frac{1}{y}-\sin \l$left(1+\frac{y}{x}\right)\left(-\frac{y}{x^2}\right)\right]$\\
$+\left(-\frac{y}{x^2}\right)  \left[\sin \frac{x}{y}+\cos \l$left(1+\frac{y}{x}\right)\right]$\\
x $\frac{\partial z}{\partial x$x}=y  \left[\frac{1}{y} \cos $\frac{x}{y}+\frac{y}{x^2} \sin \l$left(1+\frac{y}{x}\right)\right]$\\
$-\frac{y}{x}  \left[\sin \frac{x}{y}+\cos \l$left(1+\frac{y}{x}\right)\right]$\\
\Rightarrow \quad x $\frac{\partial z}{\partial x}=\cos \frac{x}{y}+\frac{y^2}{x^2} \sin \l$left(1+\frac{y}{x}\right)-$z
\end{array} Similarly, y $\frac{\partial z}{\partial y}=-\cos \frac{x}{y}-\frac{y^2}{x^2} \sin \l$left(1+\frac{y}{x}\right)+$z On adding Eqs. (i) and (ii) x $\frac{\partial z}{\partial x}=-$y $\frac{\partial z}{\partial y}

questions.q: If $y=\sqrt{x+\sqrt{y+\sqrt{x+\sqrt{y+\ldots \infty}}}}$, then $\frac{d y}{d x}=$
questions.solution: We have $\begin{aligned}$& y=$\sqrt{x+\sqrt{y+\sqrt{x+\sqrt{y+\ldots \infty}}}}$\\ & y=$\sqrt{x+\sqrt{y+y}} \Rightarrow$y^2=x+$\sqrt{2 y}$\\ \Rightarrow & y²-x=$\sqrt{2 y} \Rightarrow\left($y^2-x\right)^2=2 y \\ \Rightarrow & y⁴-2 x y²+x²=2 y \\ \Rightarrow & y⁴-2 x y²-2 y+x²=0 \end{aligned} On differentiating w.r.t. to $x$, we get $\begin{aligned}$& 4 y³ $\frac{d y}{d x}-$2 y²-4 y x $\frac{d y}{d x}-\frac{2 d y}{d x}+$2 x=0 \\ & $\frac{d y}{d x}\left($4 y³-4 x y-2\right)=-2 x+2 y² \\ \Rightarrow \quad & $\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{y^2-x}{2 y^3-2 x y-1} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: $y=\frac{\sqrt[3]{1+3 x} \sqrt[4]{1+4 x} \sqrt[5]{1+5 x}}{\sqrt[7]{1+7 x} \sqrt[8]{1+8 x}}$. Then $\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{~d} x}$ at $x=0$ is
questions.solution: \begin{aligned}+\frac{1}{5} \log (1+5 x) & -\frac{1}{7} \log (1+7 x) \\ & -\frac{1}{8} \log (1+8 x)\end{aligned}$ Differentiating both sides w.r.t. $x$, we get $\begin{array}{r}\frac{1}{y} \cdot \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{~d} x}=\frac{1}{3} \cdot \frac{1}{1+3 x} \cdot$3+$\frac{1}{4} \cdot \frac{1}{1+4 x} \cdot$4+$\frac{1}{5} \cdot \frac{1}{1+5 x} \cdot$5 \\ -$\frac{1}{7} \cdot \frac{1}{1+7 x} \cdot$7-$\frac{1}{8} \cdot \frac{1}{1+8 x} \cdot$8 \end{array} $\begin{aligned} & \therefore \quad \frac{1}{y} \cdot \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{~d} x}=\frac{1}{1+3 x}+\frac{1}{1+4 x}+\frac{1}{1+5 x}-\frac{1}{1+7 x}-\frac{1}{1+8 x} \\ & \therefore \quad \frac{1}{1} \cdot\left(\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{~d} x}\right)_{x=0}=\frac{1}{1+0}+\frac{1}{1+0}+\frac{1}{1+0}-\frac{1}{1+0}-\frac{1}{1+0} \\ & \ldots[\text { At } x=0, y=1]\end{aligned}\Rightarrow\left(\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{~d} x}\right)_{x=0}=1$

questions.q: If $a x^2+2 h x y+b y^2=3$, then $\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}=$
options: $\frac{\left(a x y+h x^2+b y x\right)}{(a x+b y)^2}$
questions.solution: We have, a x²+2 h x y+b y²=3 On differentiating with respect to $x$, we get $\begin{aligned}$& 2 a x+2 h x $\frac{d y}{d x}+$2 h y+2 b y $\frac{d y}{d x}=$0 \\ & $\frac{d y}{d x}=-\frac{(a x+h y)}{(b y+h x)} \end{aligned}$Again differentiating with respect to $x$, we get $\begin{aligned}$& 2 a+2 h x $\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}+$2 h $\frac{d y}{d x}+$2 h $\frac{d y}{d x}+$2 b\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2 \\ \text{ and } +2 b y $\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}=$0 \end{aligned} $\begin{aligned}$ \text{ and } $\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}($h x+b y)=-\left($a+2 h $\frac{d y}{d x}+$b\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2\right) \\ \text{ and } $\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}($h x+b y)= \\ \text{ and } -\left($a+2 h\left(\frac{-a x-h y}{h x+b y}\right)+$b\left(\frac{-a x-h y}{h x+b y}\right)^2\right) \end{aligned} $\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}(h x+b y)=-\left[\frac{a(h x+b y)^2-2 h(a x+h y)(h x+b y)+b(a x+h y)^2}{(h x+b y)^2}\right] \frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}=\frac{3\left(h^2-a b\right)}{(h x+b y)^3}

questions.q: If $y^{\cos x}=x^{\sin y}$, then $\frac{d y}{d x}=$
options: $\frac{y(x \sin x \log y+\sin y)}{x(\cos x-y \log x \cos y)}$
$\frac{y(x \sin x \log x-\sin y)}{x(\cos x+y \log x \cos y)}$
questions.solution: It is given that $y^{\cos x}=x^{\sin y}$ On taking logrithm both sides, we get $\cos x \log y=\sin y \log x$ On differentiating both side w.r.t. $x$, we get $\frac{1}{y}(\cos x) \frac{d y}{d x}-(\sin x) \log y=\frac{1}{x} \sin y+(\log x)(\cos y) \frac{d}{d x}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}\left(\frac{1}{y} \cos x-(\log x) \cos y\right)=\frac{1}{x} \sin y+(\sin x) \log y \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{y(\sin y+x \sin x \log y)}{x(\cos x-y \log x \cos y)}\end{aligned}$

Given that, x=a\left(\cos \theta+\log \tan \left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right)\right) \text { and }$y=a \sin $\theta$On differentiating w.r.t. $\theta$ respectively, we get $\begin{aligned}\frac{d x}{d \theta}$& =a  \left(-\sin \theta+\frac{1}{\tan \left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right)} $\cdot \sec ^2 $\frac{\theta}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{2}\right)\\
& =a\left(-\sin \$theta+\frac{1}{\sin \theta}\right)=\frac{a \cos ^2 \theta}{\sin \theta}
\end{aligned}$and $\frac{d y}{d \theta}=a \cos $\theta
$\begin{aligned}
\therefore \quad \frac{d y}{d x}$& $=\frac{d y / d \theta}{d x / d \theta}=\frac{a \cos \theta}{a \cos ^2 \theta / \sin \theta}$\\
& =\tan \theta
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $y^{2}=a x^{2}+b x+c, \quad$ where $\quad a, b, c$ are constants, then $y^{3} \frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}$ is equal to
questions.solution: Given, $y^{2}=a x^{2}+b x+c$ On differentiating w.r.t. $x$, we get $2 y \frac{d y}{d x}=2 a x+b$ Again differentiating w.r.t. $x$, we get $\begin{aligned}$& 2\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^{2}+$2 y $\frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}=$2 a \\ \Rightarrow \text{ and } y $\frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}=$a-\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^{2} \end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad y \frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}=a-\left(\frac{2 a x+b}{2 y}\right)^{2}\Rightarrow \quad y \frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}=\frac{4 a y^{2}-(2 a x+b)^{2}}{4 y^{2}}\Rightarrow \quad 4 y^{3} \frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}=4 a\left(a x^{2}+b x+c\right)-\left(4 a^{2} x^{2}+4 a b x+b^{2}\right)\Rightarrow \quad 4 y^{3} \frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}=4 a c-b^{2}\Rightarrow \quad y^{3} \frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}=\frac{4 a c-b^{2}}{4}=$ constant

questions.q: If $x=\frac{1-t^{2}}{1+t^{2}}$ and $y=\frac{2 a t}{1+t^{2}}$, then $\frac{d y}{d x}$ is equal to
questions.solution: Given, $x=\frac{1-t^{2}}{1+t^{2}}$ and $y=\frac{2 a t}{1+t^{2}}$ On differentiating w.r.t. $t$, respectively, we get $\begin{aligned}\frac{d x}{d t}$&=$\frac{\left(1+t^{2}\right)(0-2 t)-\left(1-t^{2}\right)(0+2 t)}{\left(1+t^{2}\right)^{2}}$\\ &=$\frac{-4 t}{\left(1+t^{2}\right)^{2}} \end{aligned}$and $\frac{d y}{d t}=\frac{\left(1+t^{2}\right) 2 a-2 a t(2 t)}{\left(1+t^{2}\right)^{2}}=\frac{2 a\left(1-t^{2}\right)}{\left(1+t^{2}\right)^{2}}\therefore \quad \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{d y / d t}{d x / d t}=\frac{a\left(1-t^{2}\right)}{-2 t}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{a\left(t^{2}-1\right)}{2 t}$

questions.q: Let $ϕ ( x )$ be the inverse of the function $f ( x )$ and $f^{′}  \left(x\right) = $\dfrac{1}{1 + x^{5}},then \dfrac{d}{dx}$ϕ\left(x\right) is equal to$
questions.solution:
We have, $ϕ\left(x\right) = f^{- 1} ( x )$

$⇒ x = f [ ϕ\left(x\right) ]$

On differentiating both sides w.r.t. $x$, we get

$1 = f^{'}\left[ϕ\left(x\right)\right] . {ϕ}^{'} ( x )$

$⇒ {ϕ}^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{1}{f^{'}\left[ϕ\left(x\right)\right]}$ ...(i)

Since, $f^{′}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{1}{1 + x^{5}}$ (given)

$f^{'}\left(ϕ\left(x\right)\right) = \dfrac{1}{1 + \left[ϕ\left(x\right)\right]5}$

From Equation (i),

${ϕ}^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{1}{f^{'} [ ϕ\left(x\right) ]} = 1 + \left[ϕ\left(x\right)\right]5$

questions.q: If $y = \tan^{- 1}\left(secx - tanx\right),$ then the absolute value of 2$\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is
questions.solution:
$y = \tan^{- 1}\left(secx - tanx\right)$
$y = \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1 - sinx}{cosx}\right)$
$⇒ y = \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{{\left(cos\dfrac{x}{2} - sin\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}^{2}}{\left(\cos^{2}\dfrac{x}{2} - \sin^{2}\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}\right)$
$⇒ y = \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{cos\dfrac{x}{2} - sin\dfrac{x}{2}}{cos\dfrac{x}{2} + sin\dfrac{x}{2}}\right)$
$⇒ y = \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1 - tan\dfrac{x}{2}}{1 + tan\dfrac{x}{2}}\right)$
$⇒ y = \tan^{- 1}\left(tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{x}{2}\right)\right)$
$⇒ y = \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{x}{2}$
Differentiating with respect to $x,$ we get
$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{- 1}{2} = - 0.5$

questions.q: Let $y = x^{x^{x \ldots \infty}}$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$is equal to (given $x > 0$ )
questions.solution:
Given, $y = x^{x^{x...\infty}}$ then $y = x^{y}$

Taking $ln$ on both the sides, we get

$lny = ylnx$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{y} . \dfrac{dy}{dx} = y . \dfrac{1}{x} + \dfrac{dy}{dx} . lnx$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx}\left[\dfrac{1}{y} - ln ⁡ x\right] = \dfrac{y}{x}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y^{2}}{x ( 1 - ylnx )}$
questions.source: 99 Percentile Qs Bank for JEE Main

questions.q: If $x = \dfrac{1 - t^{2}}{1 + t^{2}}$ and $y = \dfrac{2t}{1 + t^{2}}, then\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$∵ x = \dfrac{1 - t^{2}}{1 + t^{2}}andy = \dfrac{2t}{1 + t^{2}}$

Put $t = tan ⁡ \theta$ in both the equations, we get

$x = \dfrac{1 - \tan^{2} ⁡ \theta}{1 + \tan^{2} ⁡ \theta} = cos ⁡ 2\theta$ ...(i)

and $y = \dfrac{2tan ⁡ \theta}{1 + \tan^{2} ⁡ \theta} = sin ⁡ 2\theta$ ...(ii)

On differentiating both the eqs.(i) and (ii), we get

$\dfrac{dx}{d\theta} = - 2sin ⁡ 2\thetaand\dfrac{dy}{d\theta} = 2cos ⁡ 2\theta$

Therefore, $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\dfrac{dy}{d\theta}}{\dfrac{dx}{d\theta}} = - \dfrac{cos ⁡ 2\theta}{sin ⁡ 2\theta} = - \dfrac{x}{y}$

questions.q: If& $f ( x )$ has a derivative at~$x = a,$ then $\lim_{x \to a}\dfrac{xf\left(a\right) - af\left(x\right)}{x - a}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$\lim_{x \to a}\dfrac{xf\left(a\right) - af\left(x\right)}{x - a}$

Add and subtract~$af ( a )$~

$= \lim_{x \to a}\dfrac{xf\left(a\right) - af\left(a\right) + af\left(a\right) - af\left(x\right)}{x - a}$

$= \lim_{x \to a}\dfrac{f\left(a\right)\left(x - a\right) - a\left[f\left(x\right) - f\left(a\right)\right]}{x - a}$

Separate and solve

$= \lim_{x \to a}\dfrac{f\left(a\right)\left(x - a\right)}{x - a} - \lim_{x \to a}\dfrac{a\left[f\left(x\right) - f\left(a\right)\right]}{x - a}$

As~$f ' ( a ) = \lim_{x \to a}\dfrac{f ( x ) - f ( a )}{x - a}$~(derivative of~$f ( x )$~at~$x = a$~exist)

$= f \left(a\right) - af′ \left($a\right)$

$

\dfrac{dy}{dx} =$1$
